profile.headline: Staff Software Engineer
profile.summary:
Architect, designer and builder of virtual machines, compilers, operating systems and systems software.

As a youngster I worked in computer shops, for computer game companies and on real-time telemetry systems for formula 1 racing. My undergraduate degree was in computer engineering, with a focus on digital electronic design, including asynchronous, as well as ECAD tools. I won the Edwards award for best undergraduate computer engineering student (awarded by Tom Kilburn) and an Atlas scholarship. My PhD created numerous binary translator projects that were commercialized at Transitive Technologies and eventually wound up being used in Apple's Rosetta, SGI and IBM products.

My work as a university research fellow was into virtual machines, metacircular implementations, parallelizing compilers, stream processors and compilers, network security and protocols, transactional memory and novel architectural designs in particular for many core architectures.

I moved to the bay area and put this knowledge to good use by building the next generation of virtual machines for Azul Systems with performance to go beyond their existing 864 core machines with pauseless GC supporting terabytes of RAM (C4).

Now I am a staff software engineer at Google. I was the tech lead for the Android ART runtime, leading the design and introduction of a novel low-pause time generational garbage collector and ahead-of-time compilation model. I have developed in-house Google compilers and optimization projects for Android and cloud environments, as well as working on monitoring, scalability and the kernel within Google's cloud platform. I'm a leading contributor to tools in Linux the kernel.

Specialties: virtual machines, binary translators, compilers, garbage collection, C, C++, Java, assembly languages (x86, arm, arm64, powerpc, mips), systems software, digital hardware design, ecad tool creation, GPU, networking, android, dalvik, ART, Linux, open source, operating systems.
